title: Book 3 — Thalia, Chapter 447
paragraphs: Now Periander had chosen out the sons of the leading men of Corcyra and was sending them to Sardis to be made eunuchs in order to take his revenge, since the Corcyreans had first begun the offense and had done him a deed of reckless wrong. For after Periander had killed his wife Melissa, it happened to him to experience another misfortune in addition to what had already happened, and it was this. He had by Melissa two sons, one seventeen and the other eighteen years old. Their mother's father Procles, who was despot of Epidauros, sent for these sons to visit him and entertained them kindly, as might be expected since they were the sons of his own daughter. When he was sending them back, he said in taking leave of them: “Boys, do you know who killed your mother?” The elder of the two took no notice of this saying, but the younger, whose name was Lycophron, was so greatly grieved at hearing it that when he returned to Corinth, he would neither address his father, nor speak to him when his father tried to converse with him, nor give any reply when asked questions, regarding him as the murderer of his mother. At length Periander, enraged with his son, drove him out of his house.
